title: First gameplay video, zero wishlists. What did you change that actually moved the number?
author: greenlight91
selftext:
Korean solo dev, bad English, AI helped me write this.



WW2 RTS where you can also jump in and drive any tank yourself. Steam page up for a few weeks. Posted a 50 second clip from a test match last week with the wishlist link in a comment. People clicked the link (Steam UTM shows it) and nobody wishlisted. Not a few, zero.



I code most of it with Claude, voices are ElevenLabs. Can't tell if it's the video, the page, the AI smell, or the game. If you got past this phase, what was the one thing that worked?

comments.author: aura-32
comments.body:
If the UTM shows clicks but zero wishlists, the store page is the first thing I'd look at, because the video already did its job of getting people there. A few things that tend to matter most:

- The capsule image and the first two or three screenshots. Most visitors decide from those and never scroll.
- The very first seconds of the trailer on the page. Your unique hook is jumping in and driving any tank yourself, so I'd open with that moment, not the wide strategy view.
- The short description. One plain sentence that says what makes it different from other WW2 RTS games.

It can also help to open the pages of two or three similar games that are doing well and put yours side by side with them. Differences jump out fast that way. Also, a handful of clicks with no wishlists is a small sample, so don't read too much into one post.

replies.author: greenlight91
replies.body: Thanks for reading through it, and for the thoughtful reply. You're right about the store page. What's up there now is still the beta version, and it no longer matches the current build. I'll fix it right away and make sure the page leads with what makes this game different.
